messages:
maria: Quick question — we're designing the rerank endpoint semantics for candidate pruning + score expansion. thinking about two knobs: `prune_threshold` (drop candidates below X) and `score_mode` (raw | normalized | percentile). how should routing/quotas treat pruned candidates?

sam: My gut: if we prune client-side before sending to model, it should not count toward model fanout/quota. if model sees candidates and prunes server-side, it should be counted.

maria: Agreed. but product wants a simple single param that users can set and expect consistent billing/telemetry.

kevin: Console UX note: we need to show in the UI whether pruning happened pre- or post-model. otherwise customers will be confused why billed units != input count. maybe a small badge per request: "pruned: client" / "pruned: server".

anya: Telemetry implications: in our metrics we currently log `input_candidates` and `model_candidates_dispatched`. We should add `pruned_candidates_client` and `pruned_candidates_model`. also add `score_mode` to request tags so we can break down latencies by scoring semantics.

sam: Also: if `score_mode=percentile` we need to compute percentiles consistently across models. that implies we either normalize on a global distribution per-model (expensive) or use a rolling window histogram. we should document that percentile semantics are approximate.

maria: Proposal: default is `score_mode=normalized` (linear rescale to 0..1 using per-model min/max from recent window), `prune_threshold` default 0.0 (no pruning). client-side pruning only allowed if `prune_client=true` and then we don't count pruned inputs for billing.

ryan: Billing/legal: we need a clear rule in TOS. If user flips `prune_client=true` and their SDK prunes locally we can't audit their local counts. probably fine if we say "billing based on the number of candidates received by our serving layer".

kevin: Console change: add a small tooltip copy: "Billing is based on candidates dispatched to our model pool — client-side pruning reduces dispatch but may not be auditable." we should show sample dashboard tile: `dispatched_candidates / input_candidates` ratio.

anya: For telemetry pipeline: add new event `rerank.request.summary` with fields: `input_candidates`, `pruned_client`, `pruned_server`, `dispatched`, `score_mode`, `topk_returned`. all are ints/strings — we'll store as tags in events.

sam: Routing question: when we have fallback model routes (cheap quantized model then higher-quality model), do pruned candidates follow the same path? e.g., prune before fallback step to avoid extra fanout?

maria: I'd prefer to apply pruning before routing to reduce unnecessary fanout. but that changes semantics of fallbacks — smaller candidate set may change recall. product wants this optional.

ryan: Suggestion: introduce `prune_phase` param: `pre_routing` | `post_routing` | `model_decision`. default `pre_routing` if `prune_client=true` else `model_decision`.

kevin: UX for rollouts: when we flip `prune_phase` default we should add console banner explaining potential recall changes and provide a canary toggle.

deploy-bot: canary deploy for rerank-service config flags scheduled: 2023-07-20T18:30:00Z by infra-team. :shipit:

anya: For metrics, add a gauge for `effective_fanout` that is `sum(dispatched across models) / requests`. will help show savings from pre-routing prune.

sam: Edge-case: if user requests `score_mode=raw` then normalized/percentile ops should be skipped, but we must still provide `signed_scores` in telemetry. Also need to be explicit about floating precision and rounding for billing determinism.

maria: Decision draft (for eng review):
- billing: count = candidates received by serving runtime (string). client-side prune reduces billing only if pruned before runtime.
- score modes: `raw`, `normalized` (default), `percentile` (approx). documented tradeoffs.
- prune_phase param introduced; default depends on client/server config.
- telemetry: new fields + dashboard tiles to show pruning vs dispatch.
- rollout: start with canary, console banner, and a rollback playbook.

kevin: I'll pick up the console bits (banner, tile, canary toggle). I'll mock copy for tooltip.

anya: I'll add telemetry events and update the alerting dashboard to include `effective_fanout` and a regression alert if fanout increases >10% post-rollout.

sam: I'll add server enforcement for counting and simple percentiles via t-digest on the model-side. also add a compatibility header `X-Rerank-Score-Mode` on responses for debug.

maria: Nice. action items: @kevin console; @anya telemetry & alerts; @sam runtime + docs; @ryan legal/billing note. I'll write the PR RFC and ping infra for canary.

ryan: I'll file a short billing policy note and sync with finance.

maria: Thanks all — will update thread with RFC link. short follow-up: do we want a UI toggle to let customers pick "bill by input" vs "bill by dispatched"? seems risky but asked by 2 customers.

kevin: If we surface it, default must be conservative (bill by dispatched). we can show estimated cost in console pre-change.

sam: Engineering complexity is moderate — we can support an opt-in toggle but need to enforce dispatch counts server-side. prefer product to limit rollout to enterprise tiers.

maria: OK leaving as enterprise opt-in. I'll include that in the RFC. thanks.
